Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the officer/director HIPAA eligibility screen and confidentiality-training attestation at every appointment or board-seat renewal; escalates conflicts to General Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 164.530(e) (workforce sanctions policy, extended to officers/directors with oversight of PHI systems) and 164.530(b) (training requirement), re-read against the current HHS OCR Privacy Rule text at each appointment cycle

In-scope processes.value: Onboarding and re-appointment of every officer, director and Compliance/Privacy Committee member who has oversight authority over, or standing access rights to, the Group Health plan's PHI systems and privacy governance decisions

In-scope systems.value: Officer/director onboarding workflow and attestation record; HIPAA confidentiality training completion tracked in the learning management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Officer & Director HIPAA Eligibility and Training Attestation Procedure — LEIE exclusion screen, conflict-of-interest disclosure, confidentiality training, sign-off before PHI-adjacent access is provisioned

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by General Counsel; reviewed annually and on any change to the HHS OIG exclusion-screening or HIPAA training curriculum

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per appointment — eligibility screen, conflict disclosure and confidentiality/HIPAA training attestation must all close within 30 days of the appointment or board seat becoming effective; unresolved conflicts escalated within 60 days

Deadline reminders configured.value: HRIS onboarding task reminders fire at day 15 and day 25 after appointment date, with an automatic access-hold flag at day 30 if incomplete

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed attestation, LEIE screen result and any conflict-waiver memo retained 6 years from the end of the officer's or director's tenure, per the HIPAA documentation retention standard at 164.530(j)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Attestations still open at day 30 are logged as exceptions and the officer's PHI-system access is held until General Counsel clears the exception

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every conflict-of-interest waiver and every attestation completed after the 30-day window

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every officer and director appointment or re-appointment with an effective date inside the test period, per the board and committee membership roster maintained by the Corporate Secretary

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any officer or director who received PHI-system or governance access before eligibility screen and training were both complete is a fail; any fail is escalated to General Counsel the same week

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-appointment; test runs quarterly over that quarter's appointment population plus 100% review of any new board seat

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have processed any sampled appointment's onboarding

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly officer/director eligibility test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Attestation register export plus LEIE screen results and training completion certificates, presentable to HHS OCR within 5 business days of a request

Regulator response path.value: Privacy Officer owns the OCR inquiry response; General Counsel clears any statement about a specific officer's clearance status before it is sent

checklist.step: Identify every officer and director requiring a fitness assessment this cycle
actions: In the HRIS open the Board & Officer Roster report and filter New/Renewing = Yes for the current period.
Cross-check the filtered list against the Corporate Secretary's board and Compliance Committee membership register.
For each name, record appointment date, seat/title, and whether the role carries standing PHI-system access.
Open an onboarding case in the HRIS workflow for each name with a due date 30 calendar days from the appointment date.
checklist.done: every new or renewing officer/director has an open HRIS onboarding case with an appointment date and a 30-day due date.

checklist.step: Collect the eligibility and conflict-of-interest disclosure
actions: Send the standard Officer/Director Eligibility & Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure form to the individual through the HRIS onboarding case.
Confirm the form covers: other health-plan or PHI-related board seats held, family/financial interests in vendors or providers, and any prior HIPAA violation finding against them.
Chase non-response at day 10 and again at day 20 against the 30-day clock.
Attach the signed disclosure to the onboarding case file.
checklist.done: a signed eligibility and conflict-of-interest disclosure is attached to the onboarding case.

checklist.step: Screen the individual against the HHS OIG exclusion list
actions: Search the individual's full legal name and date of birth on the HHS OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) online database.
Also search the SAM.gov federal exclusions list for a corroborating hit.
Save a dated screenshot or export of the search result (no match / match requiring review) into the onboarding case.
Any hit is routed immediately to General Counsel — do not continue onboarding pending clearance.
checklist.done: a dated LEIE (and SAM.gov) screen result, with no unresolved hit, is filed against the onboarding case.

checklist.step: Route disclosed conflicts to Legal for adjudication
actions: Review every disclosure that flags another board seat, a financial interest, or a prior violation finding.
Determine whether the conflict requires recusal from specific privacy-governance votes, a waiver, or is not material.
Draft the waiver or recusal memo and route it to General Counsel for countersignature.
Log the adjudication outcome on the onboarding case.
checklist.done: every disclosed conflict has a written adjudication (waiver, recusal scope, or not-material finding) on file.

checklist.step: Assign the HIPAA confidentiality and privacy-governance training module
actions: In Cornerstone LMS assign the 'HIPAA Confidentiality for Officers & Directors' curriculum to the individual's learner profile.
Set the module due date to 25 calendar days from the appointment date, 5 days ahead of the overall clock.
Confirm the curriculum includes minimum-necessary use, workforce sanctions policy, and breach-reporting duties.
Enable the LMS auto-reminder at day 15 and day 22.
checklist.done: the training module is assigned in the LMS with a due date inside the 30-day window and reminders active.

checklist.step: Track completion of screening and training against the 30-day window
actions: Update the onboarding case checklist as each item closes: disclosure received, LEIE screen clean, conflict adjudicated (if any), training complete.
Pull the HRIS onboarding dashboard weekly and sort by days-remaining-to-due-date.
Confirm no PHI-system access request has been submitted for anyone with an open item.
Flag any case reaching day 25 with open items to the HR Business Partner's manager.
checklist.done: the onboarding case shows real-time status of all four gating items against the 30-day countdown.

checklist.step: Escalate overdue attestations at day 30
actions: For any case still open at day 30, open an exception ticket in ITSM tagged 'HIPAA-Officer-Eligibility'.
Notify General Counsel and the individual's board sponsor of the overdue item and the access hold this triggers.
Record the exception reason (non-response, unresolved conflict, training incomplete) on the ticket.
Set a remediation date and assign an owner.
checklist.done: every case open past day 30 has an ITSM exception ticket with owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Hold or provision PHI-adjacent system access based on clearance status
actions: Before actioning any access request tied to a board or officer seat, check the HRIS onboarding case status.
Provision access only when disclosure, LEIE screen, conflict adjudication and training all show Complete.
Where the case is open, place the access request on hold and notify the requester of the pending gate.
Log the access decision and the case reference in the identity platform's request record.
checklist.done: no PHI-adjacent access is granted against an onboarding case that is not fully cleared.

checklist.step: Countersign the completed attestation packet
actions: Review the assembled packet: disclosure, LEIE screen, conflict adjudication (if any), and training completion certificate.
Confirm the packet is internally consistent and dated within the 30-day window (or carries an approved exception).
Countersign the attestation cover sheet.
Return the countersigned packet to HR Business Partner for filing.
checklist.done: the attestation packet carries General Counsel's dated countersignature.

checklist.step: Record the assessment outcome in the officer governance register
actions: In the board portal's governance register, add or update the entry for the individual with clearance date and status.
Link the register entry to the countersigned attestation packet in the document repository.
Note any active recusal scope from the conflict adjudication against the individual's record.
Confirm the register entry is visible to the Board Governance Lead ahead of the next board meeting.
checklist.done: the governance register shows a clearance date, status and any recusal scope for the individual.

checklist.step: Notify the Board Governance Lead that the seat is cleared to activate
actions: Send the clearance confirmation to the Board Governance Lead once the countersigned packet is filed.
Include the effective date the officer/director may begin exercising voting or oversight authority on PHI-governance matters.
Copy the individual's board sponsor and the Compliance Officer.
File the notification in the onboarding case.
checklist.done: the Board Governance Lead has a dated clearance notification before the seat is activated.

checklist.step: File the signed attestation, LEIE result and training certificate as evidence
actions: Move the disclosure, LEIE screen export, conflict memo (if any), training certificate and countersigned cover sheet into the compliance evidence repository.
File under the individual's name and appointment date, cross-referenced to the governance register entry.
Apply the 6-year-from-end-of-tenure retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by name and appointment date.
checklist.done: the full evidence set is filed in the compliance evidence repository with the retention label applied.

checklist.step: Re-screen continuing officers and directors at each renewal
actions: At each board term renewal, re-run the LEIE screen and reissue the conflict-of-interest disclosure.
Confirm HIPAA training is current (not older than the curriculum's stated refresh interval); reassign if lapsed.
Treat a renewal exactly as a new appointment for the 30-day clock and evidence set.
Update the governance register with the new clearance date.
checklist.done: every renewing officer/director has a fresh 30-day-cycle clearance on file, not a carried-forward one.

checklist.step: Manage disclosed conflicts requiring ongoing recusal
actions: Maintain a standing list of active recusal scopes from adjudicated conflicts.
Before any privacy-governance vote, check attendee list against the recusal list and instruct affected members to abstain.
Record the recusal in the meeting minutes maintained by the Corporate Secretary.
Review each active recusal annually to confirm it is still warranted.
checklist.done: every active recusal is enforced at the relevant vote and re-confirmed at least annually.

checklist.step: Retain records through the full 6-year post-tenure window
actions: On departure of an officer or director, set the retention-expiry date on their evidence file to 6 years from the departure date.
Confirm the compliance evidence repository's retention policy engine carries the correct expiry, not a default.
Run the annual retention audit to confirm no eligible file has been purged early.
Route confirmed-expired files to General Counsel for disposition approval before deletion.
checklist.done: every departed officer's/director's file carries a correct 6-year expiry and is not purged without General Counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Build the population of officer/director appointments in the test period
actions: Extract from the HRIS all new appointments and renewals with an effective date inside the quarter.
Reconcile the extract to the Corporate Secretary's board and Compliance Committee membership register for the same period.
Resolve any name on one list but not the other before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the governance register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Match each population row to a complete attestation packet
actions: For each appointment, locate the corresponding packet in the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm all four elements are present: disclosure, LEIE screen, conflict adjudication (if flagged), training certificate.
List any appointment with no packet, or a packet missing an element, as an automatic exception.
Note the packet's countersignature date for the deadline check.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a packet or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of new board seats (as opposed to routine renewals).
Take a random sample of 10 renewals, seeded and reproducible, minimum 15 rows total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every new board seat.

testing.step: Re-perform the LEIE exclusion screen for each sampled individual
actions: Independently search the HHS OIG LEIE database for each sampled individual by name and date of birth.
Compare the auditor's result to the result filed in the packet; any discrepancy is an exception.
Screenshot the auditor's own search result into the workpaper.
For any true LEIE hit, confirm it was escalated to General Counsel and resolved before access was granted.
testing.done: each sampled individual has an independently re-performed LEIE result matching the filed record, or a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify training completion against the LMS record
actions: In Cornerstone LMS pull the completion record and date for each sampled individual's HIPAA confidentiality module.
Compare the completion date to the packet's training certificate; dates must match.
Confirm the module version taken was the current curriculum, not a superseded one.
Capture the LMS completion screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: training completion in the LMS agrees with the filed certificate for every sampled row.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day clock for each sampled appointment
actions: Recompute days elapsed from appointment date to the countersignature date on the attestation cover sheet.
Flag any packet countersigned more than 30 days after appointment without a filed ITSM exception ticket.
For flagged rows, confirm access was held (not granted) during the overdue period by checking the access platform's grant timestamp.
Any access granted before full clearance is a reportable breach, not a routine exception.
testing.done: no sampled appointment shows access granted before clearance, and all clock recomputations are documented.

testing.step: Test conflict-of-interest adjudications and active recusals
actions: For every sampled individual with a disclosed conflict, read General Counsel's adjudication memo.
Pull two recent privacy-governance meeting minutes and confirm any required recusal was actually enforced.
Flag any vote where a conflicted member's abstention was not recorded.
Confirm the recusal list reviewed by General Counsel is current, not stale.
testing.done: every disclosed conflict has an adjudication on file and, where recusal was required, evidence it was enforced.

testing.step: Confirm evidence retention labelling
actions: For each sampled row, open the repository record and check the retention label reflects 6 years from tenure end (or is open for active officers).
For any departed officer in the sample, confirm the expiry date was recalculated on departure.
Spot-check that the record is retrievable by name and appointment date search.
Log any missing or incorrect retention label as an exception.
testing.done: retention labelling is correct and the record is retrievable for every sampled row.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception with the individual's name, appointment date and the specific gap.
Assign a root cause (late screening, missed training assignment, unresolved conflict, mis-filed evidence) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; for any pre-clearance access grant, open a self-assessment with General Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for pre-clearance access.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed none of the sampled onboarding cases, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual board review and approval of the HIPAA privacy policy suite; Privacy Officer prepares the package

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 164.530(i) (policies and procedures requirement) and 164.530(e) (sanctions policy), re-read against current HHS OCR guidance ahead of each annual cycle

In-scope processes.value: Annual governance review and board approval of the HIPAA Privacy Policies and Procedures suite: Notice of Privacy Practices content, minimum-necessary standard, workforce sanctions policy, and the privacy officer designation

In-scope systems.value: Policy library holds the current and prior versions with version history; approvals recorded against each policy record

Compliance procedure documented.value: HIPAA Privacy Policy Governance Procedure — annual refresh, legal review, board pack assembly, approval vote, publication

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board; procedure itself reviewed by General Counsel every 3 years or on material regulatory change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — the full policy suite must be re-approved before the anniversary of the prior approval date; interim amendments are approved at the next scheduled board or committee meeting

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform sends the Privacy Officer a review-cycle alert 90 days ahead of the approval anniversary and a board-pack-due alert 30 days ahead

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Board minutes, the approved policy version and the vote record retained 6 years from the date the policy was last in effect, per 164.530(j)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any policy still on the prior year's approved version past the anniversary date is logged as a governance exception until re-approved

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off the corrective re-approval and confirms no policy operated past its approval anniversary without one

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every HIPAA privacy policy and procedure document in the GRC policy library with an approval anniversary inside the test period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any policy operated past its annual re-approval date without a board vote is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per policy; test runs annually across the full policy suite, aligned to the board's governance calendar

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored or presented any sampled board pack

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policy governance test workpaper (population extract, board minutes cross-reference, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved policy versions plus board minutes and vote records, presentable to HHS OCR within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Privacy Officer owns the OCR inquiry response on policy governance; General Counsel clears the response before it is sent

checklist.step: Open the annual policy governance cycle 90 days ahead of the anniversary
actions: In the GRC platform pull the policy library report filtered to HIPAA Privacy policies with an approval anniversary in the next 90 days.
Open a governance-cycle case for each policy, tagged with its current version number and last approval date.
Notify General Counsel and the policy owners (Privacy Ops, HR) that the annual cycle has opened.
Set the cycle's target board-pack-due date 60 days ahead of the anniversary.
checklist.done: a governance-cycle case is open for every policy due for annual approval, with owners notified.

checklist.step: Redline each policy against current HIPAA text and prior-year exceptions
actions: Compare each policy's current text to 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E as currently published, noting any subsections added, amended or removed.
Pull the prior year's compliance-test exceptions for that policy area and confirm the redline addresses each one.
Draft redlines in tracked-changes form and route them to the relevant policy owner (e.g., HR for the sanctions policy) for factual accuracy review.
Log outstanding regulatory bulletins or OCR guidance referenced in the redline rationale.
checklist.done: each policy has a tracked-changes redline addressing regulatory text and prior exceptions.

checklist.step: Route redlines through legal review
actions: Review each redline for legal sufficiency against 164.530(i) and related sections.
Confirm the sanctions policy redline (164.530(e)) specifies a graduated sanctions schedule and a named enforcement owner.
Return unresolved comments to the Privacy Officer with a required-fix flag.
Approve the redline for board packaging once comments are cleared.
checklist.done: every redline carries a Privacy Counsel legal-sufficiency approval before packaging.

checklist.step: Assemble the board approval pack
actions: Upload the clean and redlined versions of every policy, the legal-sufficiency approval, and a one-page summary of material changes to the board portal.
Include the prior year's exception list and remediation status as an appendix.
Confirm the pack is posted at least 5 business days ahead of the scheduled board or Compliance Committee meeting per the board's governance calendar.
Send a calendar hold and pre-read notice to all voting members.
checklist.done: the board pack is posted in the board portal at least 5 business days ahead of the meeting.

checklist.step: Present the pack and record the approval vote
actions: Present the material-changes summary and answer member questions at the meeting.
Call the vote per policy (or as a bundled resolution where the board's charter allows it) and record the vote count.
Note any policy the board sends back for further revision, with the specific requested change.
Instruct the Corporate Secretary to draft the minute entry.
checklist.done: each policy has a recorded board vote outcome (approved, approved-with-condition, or returned).

checklist.step: Draft and finalize the board minutes evidencing approval
actions: Draft the minute entry naming each policy, its version number, and the vote outcome.
Circulate the draft minutes to attendees for correction within 5 business days.
Finalize and have the Chair sign the minutes.
File the signed minutes in the board portal's permanent record.
checklist.done: signed board minutes exist naming every policy and its approval outcome.

checklist.step: Publish the approved policy version and retire the prior version
actions: In the GRC platform, set the approved redline as the new current version with the board approval date as the effective date.
Mark the prior version superseded and lock it from further edits.
Push the update notification to workforce members via the intranet policy hub.
Update the policy's next-anniversary date to one year from the new approval date.
checklist.done: the GRC record shows the new version as current, the prior version as superseded, and the next-anniversary date reset.

checklist.step: Rework and re-route any policy the board returned
actions: Address the board's specific requested change in a new redline within 10 business days.
Re-route through Privacy Counsel for legal sufficiency.
Schedule the reworked policy for approval at the next scheduled meeting, not left pending indefinitely.
Track the returned policy as open in the governance-cycle case until re-approved.
checklist.done: every returned policy is reworked and back on a board agenda within one meeting cycle.

checklist.step: Cascade the approved sanctions policy to HR enforcement
actions: Confirm the newly approved sanctions schedule matches what is loaded into the HR disciplinary action workflow.
Update the workforce handbook reference and any manager-facing sanctions job aid.
Brief HR investigators on any change to the sanctions schedule or enforcement owner.
Log the cascade completion date against the policy's governance-cycle case.
checklist.done: the HR enforcement workflow reflects the newly approved sanctions schedule.

checklist.step: Confirm downstream procedure documents are updated to match
actions: Review each operating procedure that implements a board-approved policy (e.g., DSAR handling, minimum-necessary checklists).
Update any procedure whose language or thresholds changed in the new policy version.
Route procedure updates through the standard change-control process, referencing the policy version and approval date.
Confirm the procedure library shows the same effective date as the policy.
checklist.done: every dependent procedure cites the current policy version and effective date.

checklist.step: Notify the workforce of the material changes
actions: Draft a plain-language summary of what changed and why.
Distribute via the workforce communication channel used for compliance notices.
For changes affecting daily workflow (e.g., sanctions, minimum necessary), require an acknowledgment click-through.
Track acknowledgment completion and escalate non-responders to their manager after 10 business days.
checklist.done: the workforce notice is distributed and acknowledgment tracking is active.

checklist.step: Update training content to reflect the approved policy
actions: Revise the HIPAA privacy workforce training module to reflect the new policy language and effective date.
Route the revised module through Privacy Counsel for accuracy sign-off before publishing.
Publish the updated module in the LMS and version-stamp it.
Confirm any workforce member due for refresher training receives the updated version, not the retired one.
checklist.done: the LMS module is version-stamped to the current policy and no learner is assigned the retired version.

checklist.step: Log any policy operating past its anniversary without approval
actions: Run the anniversary-date report weekly during the cycle window.
For any policy past its anniversary with no recorded board vote, open a governance exception in the GRC platform.
Escalate to General Counsel and the Board Governance Lead the same week.
Track the exception to closure with a corrective re-approval date.
checklist.done: no policy sits past its anniversary date without either an approval or a logged, escalated exception.

checklist.step: Archive the superseded version and the full approval trail
actions: Move the superseded policy version, redlines, legal sign-off, board pack and signed minutes into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year-from-last-effective retention label.
Cross-reference the archive entry to the new current version for full lineage.
Confirm the archive is searchable by policy name and version.
checklist.done: the full approval trail is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by policy name and version.

checklist.step: Confirm the next cycle's calendar entry before closing this cycle
actions: Verify the GRC platform's next-anniversary date and 90-day alert are set for every policy just approved.
Confirm the board's governance calendar carries a placeholder agenda item for next year's cycle.
Close the current governance-cycle case with the final approval date and vote reference.
Hand off any open action items to next year's cycle owner.
checklist.done: the next cycle is calendared and this cycle's case is closed with a final approval reference.

testing.step: Build the population of policies due for annual approval
actions: Extract every HIPAA Privacy policy record from the GRC library with an anniversary date inside the test period.
Reconcile the extract to the board's governance calendar agenda items for the same period.
Resolve any policy on one list but not the other before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the board calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Match each policy to a recorded board vote before its anniversary
actions: For each population row, locate the board minutes recording the approval vote.
Confirm the vote date is on or before the policy's anniversary date.
List any policy with no matching vote, or a vote after the anniversary, as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a timely board vote or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of policies with a material-change redline this cycle.
Take a random sample of unchanged (administrative-refresh) policies, minimum 5 rows, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every materially changed policy.

testing.step: Re-perform the legal-sufficiency check on sampled redlines
actions: Independently compare each sampled policy's approved text to the current 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E text.
Confirm the sanctions policy specifies a graduated schedule and named enforcement owner.
Compare findings to Privacy Counsel's legal-sufficiency sign-off; any gap is an exception.
Note the specific subsection if a regulatory requirement is not reflected in the policy text.
testing.done: each sampled policy's text is independently confirmed sufficient, or a gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify board minutes support the vote outcome
actions: Pull the signed minutes for each sampled policy's approval meeting from the board portal.
Confirm the minutes name the policy, version number and vote count, and are Chair-signed.
Confirm the board pack was posted at least 5 business days ahead of the meeting per the portal's timestamp.
Capture the minutes and posting timestamp into the workpaper.
testing.done: signed, timely-posted minutes support the vote outcome for every sampled policy.

testing.step: Trace publication and version control
actions: Confirm the GRC record shows the approved version as current with the correct effective date.
Confirm the prior version is marked superseded and locked.
Check the next-anniversary date was reset to one year from the new approval date.
Flag any policy still showing the prior version as current past the approval date.
testing.done: version control in the GRC platform matches the board-approved outcome for every sampled policy.

testing.step: Verify workforce cascade for sampled material changes
actions: For sampled policies with material change, confirm the workforce notice was distributed and acknowledgment tracking shows a completion rate.
Confirm the LMS training module version-stamp matches the new policy's effective date.
Sample 5 workforce members due for refresher training and confirm none was assigned the retired module.
Log any lag between policy approval and training/notice cascade exceeding 30 days as an exception.
testing.done: workforce cascade and training currency are confirmed for every sampled material change, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute anniversary-date compliance across the full population
actions: For every policy in the population, recompute days between the prior approval date and this cycle's approval date.
Flag any gap exceeding 366 days as a lapse in annual re-approval.
Cross-check flagged policies against the GRC governance-exception log to confirm they were caught and escalated.
Any lapse not caught by the process itself is a control-design finding, not just an instance exception.
testing.done: no policy shows a re-approval gap exceeding 366 days without a logged, escalated exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an exception record per finding with the policy name, gap description and impact.
Assign a root cause (calendar miss, legal review delay, board scheduling) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any policy that lapsed, require an out-of-cycle board approval.
Carry open exceptions into next year's cycle as mandatory retest items.
testing.done: every exception has a record, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance annual re-approval threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled board pack, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns publication and delivery of the Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) at every trigger point for the Group Health plan

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 164.520(a)-(c) (content, revision and delivery of the NPP for group health plans), read alongside 164.520(c)(1)(v) (triennial availability reminder), re-verified against current HHS OCR text ahead of each cycle

In-scope processes.value: NPP delivery at initial enrollment, upon any individual's request, within 60 days of a material revision, and the triennial reminder of NPP availability to all enrollees

In-scope systems.value: NPP is posted on the member self-service portal and mailed via the enrollment fulfillment workflow; distribution events logged in the notice-tracking log

Compliance procedure documented.value: NPP Publication and Delivery Procedure — trigger identification, content review, mailing/posting execution, distribution logging

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Privacy Counsel; reviewed annually and whenever the NPP content itself is revised

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — NPP delivered at enrollment (with the enrollment packet), material revisions posted and mailed within 60 days of the revision's effective date, availability reminder issued at least once every 3 years to all enrollees

Deadline reminders configured.value: Notice-tracking log fires a 60-day countdown on any content revision and a rolling 3-year countdown per enrollee cohort for the availability reminder

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Distribution logs, mailing manifests and the version of the NPP in effect at each distribution retained 6 years per 164.530(j)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any enrollment processed without a logged NPP delivery, or a revision not distributed inside 60 days, is logged as an exception with a cure date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Privacy Counsel signs off any late distribution remediation and any decision that a change was not 'material' and did not require redistribution

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All new enrollments, all NPP content revisions, and any enrollee cohort due its triennial reminder inside the test period, per the enrollment system and notice-tracking log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any enrollment with no logged NPP delivery, or any material revision not distributed within 60 days, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; test runs quarterly over the quarter's enrollments and revisions, plus an annual check of the rolling triennial-reminder cohort

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have processed any sampled enrollment or distribution

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly NPP distribution test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Distribution log export plus mailing manifests and the NPP version history, presentable to HHS OCR within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Privacy Officer owns the OCR inquiry response on notice practices; Privacy Counsel clears the response before it is sent

checklist.step: Identify every NPP trigger event occurring this cycle
actions: Pull the new-enrollment report from the enrollment system for the period.
Pull the notice-tracking log's rolling triennial-reminder report to identify enrollee cohorts due this cycle.
Check whether any NPP content revision was approved this cycle via the policy governance record.
Compile a single trigger worklist covering enrollment, revision and reminder events.
checklist.done: a worklist exists covering every enrollment, revision and reminder trigger due this cycle.

checklist.step: Confirm the current NPP content is accurate before distribution
actions: Read the current NPP against 164.520(b) required content elements: uses/disclosures, individual rights, plan duties, complaint process, effective date.
Confirm the effective date on the NPP matches the last board-approved policy version.
Flag any content drift between the NPP and the underlying approved privacy policy for correction before distribution.
Approve the current version for distribution or route corrections back to the Privacy Officer.
checklist.done: the NPP version to be distributed is confirmed accurate and Privacy-Counsel approved.

checklist.step: Deliver the NPP with every new enrollment packet
actions: Confirm the enrollment fulfillment workflow attaches the current NPP version to every new-enrollee packet, mailed or electronic.
For electronic delivery, confirm the enrollee's e-delivery consent is on file per 164.520(c)(3) before substituting mail with email.
Spot-check 5 packets generated this week for the correct NPP version attached.
Log each enrollment's NPP delivery event (channel, date, version) in the notice-tracking log.
checklist.done: every new enrollment this cycle has a logged NPP delivery event with channel, date and version.

checklist.step: Fulfill individual requests for the NPP
actions: Log every member request for a copy of the NPP received by phone, portal message or mail in the notice-tracking log.
Send the current NPP version within the plan's stated service standard (same business day for portal requests, 5 business days for mail).
Confirm the format matches the request (large print, translated version) where the plan has one available.
Close the request record with the fulfillment date and channel.
checklist.done: every logged NPP request shows a fulfillment date within the stated service standard.

checklist.step: Assess whether an approved policy change is a 'material' NPP revision
actions: Compare the approved policy change to the current NPP content elements to see if it changes a stated use, disclosure, right or duty.
Apply the 164.520(b)(3) materiality standard and document the determination with rationale.
Where material, set the NPP revision effective date and start the 60-day distribution clock.
Where not material, log the determination without triggering redistribution.
checklist.done: every approved policy change has a documented materiality determination.

checklist.step: Republish the revised NPP and post it prominently
actions: Replace the NPP document on the member self-service portal's Privacy Practices page with the new version.
Post the revised NPP at any physical service location where the plan is required to post it.
Update the effective date and version number visible on the document.
Log the posting date and locations.
checklist.done: the revised NPP is live on the portal and posted at required locations with a logged date.

checklist.step: Mail or electronically deliver the revised NPP to enrollees within 60 days
actions: Pull the current enrollee mailing/e-delivery list from the enrollment system.
Generate the distribution batch (mail house file or e-delivery batch) referencing the new NPP version.
Confirm the batch completes and enrollees receive the notice within 60 days of the revision's effective date.
Log the batch completion date and enrollee count in the notice-tracking log.
checklist.done: the revised NPP reaches all enrollees within 60 days of its effective date, logged with count and date.

checklist.step: Issue the triennial availability reminder to due cohorts
actions: Identify enrollee cohorts whose last NPP reminder (or initial delivery) was 3 years or more ago.
Generate the reminder communication stating the NPP is available and how to obtain a copy.
Distribute via the plan's standard annual mailing or e-delivery channel.
Log the reminder distribution date per cohort and reset the 3-year clock.
checklist.done: every cohort due its triennial reminder receives one, logged with a reset 3-year clock.

checklist.step: Verify e-delivery consent is on file before substituting electronic delivery
actions: For any enrollee receiving the NPP electronically, confirm an affirmative e-delivery consent record exists per 164.520(c)(3).
Where no consent is on file, route the enrollee to mail delivery instead.
Confirm the consent record includes the right to obtain a paper copy on request.
Log the consent check outcome against the delivery event.
checklist.done: no electronic-only NPP delivery occurs without a logged, valid e-delivery consent.

checklist.step: Handle requests for confidential communications alongside NPP delivery
actions: Where an enrollee requests an alternative address or channel for NPP and related communications, log the request per 164.522(b).
Accommodate the request without requiring an explanation, updating the delivery channel on the enrollee's record.
Confirm subsequent distribution batches pull the updated channel preference.
Log the accommodation date.
checklist.done: alternative-communication requests are logged and reflected in the next distribution batch.

checklist.step: Reconcile the distribution log to the enrollment and revision triggers
actions: Weekly, compare new enrollments in the enrollment system to logged NPP delivery events in the notice-tracking log.
Flag any enrollment with no matching delivery event within 2 business days of enrollment.
Route flagged gaps to the Privacy Officer for same-week remediation.
Record the reconciliation outcome for the period.
checklist.done: every enrollment is reconciled to a logged NPP delivery event within 2 business days, with gaps remediated.

checklist.step: Escalate any distribution that will miss its statutory window
actions: Monitor the 60-day revision clock and the rolling 3-year reminder clock for at-risk items.
Where a batch is at risk of missing the window, escalate to the Privacy Officer and mailing vendor the same week.
Document the cause of delay and the corrective distribution date.
Confirm the corrective distribution actually completes before closing the escalation.
checklist.done: no NPP distribution misses its statutory window without a documented, closed escalation.

checklist.step: File distribution evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the distribution log extract, mailing manifest and the exact NPP version distributed into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year retention label from the distribution date.
Cross-reference the archive entry to the trigger event (enrollment batch, revision, reminder cohort).
Confirm the archive is searchable by trigger type and date.
checklist.done: distribution evidence is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by trigger type and date.

checklist.step: Report the cycle's distribution completeness to the Privacy Officer's leadership
actions: Summarize delivery counts, any exceptions, and their remediation status for the cycle.
Present the summary at the next privacy governance meeting.
Note any systemic gap (e.g., a vendor feed missing enrollees) for corrective action ownership.
File the summary alongside the cycle's evidence.
checklist.done: a cycle summary with counts and exception status is presented and filed.

checklist.step: Confirm the next cycle's triggers are calendared before closing
actions: Verify the notice-tracking log's rolling 3-year cohort calendar is current for all enrollees processed this cycle.
Confirm any pending policy revision not yet material is queued for reassessment at next approval.
Close the cycle's trigger worklist with final delivery counts.
Hand off any open item to the next cycle owner.
checklist.done: the next cycle's triggers are calendared and this cycle's worklist is closed with final counts.

testing.step: Build the population of NPP trigger events in the test period
actions: Extract all new enrollments from the enrollment system for the quarter.
Extract all NPP revision determinations and triennial-reminder cohorts due in the quarter from the notice-tracking log.
Reconcile enrollment counts to the plan's membership system for the same period.
Sign the reconciled population count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the membership system and signed as complete.

testing.step: Match each trigger event to a logged distribution
actions: Match each enrollment, revision and reminder-cohort row to a delivery log entry with date, channel and version.
Confirm the delivery date falls inside the statutory window (at enrollment, within 60 days of revision, within the rolling 3-year reminder cycle).
List unmatched or late rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a timely, logged distribution or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of NPP revision distributions this period.
Take a random sample of 30 enrollment deliveries and 10 reminder-cohort deliveries, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers all revision distributions.

testing.step: Re-perform the NPP content review on the version distributed
actions: Open the exact NPP version referenced on each sampled delivery log entry.
Independently confirm it contains all 164.520(b) required content elements and the correct effective date.
Any missing element or stale effective date is an exception, not a documentation gap.
Note findings on the workpaper with the version identifier.
testing.done: each sampled distributed version is independently confirmed content-complete, or a gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace enrollment deliveries to the enrollment record and channel consent
actions: For each sampled enrollment, confirm the enrollee's record shows enrollment date and the NPP delivery event.
For electronic deliveries, confirm a valid e-delivery consent record exists dated before the delivery.
Capture the enrollment and delivery screens into the workpaper.
Flag any electronic delivery with no consent on file as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled enrollment traces to a delivery event with valid consent where electronic, or a logged exception.

testing.step: Recompute the 60-day revision-distribution window
actions: For each sampled revision distribution, recompute days between the revision's effective date and the batch completion date.
Flag any gap exceeding 60 days.
Cross-check flagged rows against the escalation log to confirm they were caught and remediated.
Note the final corrective distribution date where applicable.
testing.done: no sampled revision distribution exceeds 60 days without a logged, remediated escalation.

testing.step: Recompute the rolling 3-year reminder cycle
actions: For each sampled reminder-cohort row, recompute the gap between the last delivery/reminder date and this cycle's reminder date.
Flag any cohort exceeding 3 years (1,096 days) between reminders.
Confirm the notice-tracking log reset the clock correctly after this cycle's reminder.
Log any lapse as an exception.
testing.done: no sampled cohort exceeds the 3-year reminder window without a logged exception and corrected reset.

testing.step: Verify confidential-communication accommodations were honored
actions: Pull 5 sampled enrollees with an active alternative-communication request on file.
Confirm the most recent NPP distribution to them used the accommodated channel/address.
Flag any distribution that reverted to the default channel despite an active accommodation.
Log findings against the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled accommodation requests are confirmed honored in the most recent distribution, or logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a case per exception with the trigger type, enrollee/cohort identifier and the specific gap.
Assign a root cause (feed gap, vendor delay, consent not captured, materiality misjudged) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and confirm corrective distribution actually completes.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a case, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed statutory windows.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed no sampled distribution, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns intake, evaluation and SLA tracking of amendment and restriction requests received from Group Health members

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 164.526 (amendment of PHI, 60-day action window with one 30-day extension) and 164.522(a) (right to request restriction), re-read against current HHS OCR text at each procedure review

In-scope processes.value: Member requests to amend PHI in the designated record set, and member requests to restrict uses/disclosures of PHI, from intake through decision, notification and (for amendments) downstream notice to prior recipients

In-scope systems.value: DSAR/amendment/restriction case queue tracks intake date, decision, notification date and SLA status

Compliance procedure documented.value: Amendment and Restriction Request Handling Procedure — intake, designated-record-set lookup, decision criteria, denial letter content, notification of downstream recipients

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Privacy Counsel; reviewed annually and on any HHS OCR guidance update on the amendment/restriction rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Amendment requests: act within 60 days of receipt, with one permitted 30-day extension if the member is notified in writing of the reason and new date; restriction requests: acknowledge and decide without an undue delay, tracked to a 30-day internal SLA

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case queue fires reminders at day 45 and day 55 on amendment requests approaching the 60-day deadline, and at day 20 on restriction requests approaching the internal 30-day SLA

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Request record, decision rationale, denial letter (if any) and notification confirmations retained 6 years per 164.530(j)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any amendment request undecided past 60/90 days, or restriction request left undecided past the internal SLA, is logged as an exception with a cure date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Privacy Counsel signs off every denial letter and every SLA breach remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All amendment and restriction requests logged in the case queue with a receipt date inside the test period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any amendment request decided (or extended) after 60/90 days without a compliant extension notice is a fail; any restriction request left undecided past the internal SLA without documented cause is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per request; test runs monthly over the full population of requests closed or still open in that month

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have worked any sampled request

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly amendment/restriction SLA test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Case queue export with decision dates and denial letters, presentable to HHS OCR within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Privacy Officer owns the OCR complaint response; Privacy Counsel clears any specific-member response before it is sent

checklist.step: Log the incoming amendment or restriction request
actions: Open a new case in the case management tool tagged AMENDMENT or RESTRICTION with the request channel (portal, mail, phone).
Record the member's identity, the specific PHI or disclosure the request targets, and the receipt date.
Verify the requester's identity against the member's enrollment record before proceeding.
Send the member an acknowledgment within 5 business days confirming the case number and the applicable statutory clock.
checklist.done: a logged case exists with verified requester identity, receipt date and an acknowledgment sent within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Locate the PHI in the designated record set
actions: Identify every system holding the targeted PHI within the designated record set (claims, enrollment, care management notes).
Pull the current record(s) and attach a copy to the case as the baseline for the decision.
Note who created the record and whether it originated with the plan or a third party (e.g., a provider).
Confirm the record is still within the plan's designated record set as defined in the privacy policy.
checklist.done: the targeted PHI record is located, copied into the case, and its source confirmed.

checklist.step: Apply the amendment decision criteria (for AMENDMENT cases)
actions: Check whether the record was created by the plan itself and is part of the designated record set (a threshold requirement to grant).
Check whether the record is accurate and complete as-is, which is grounds to deny under 164.526(a)(2).
Where the plan did not create the record, confirm whether the originator is reasonably available to amend it instead.
Draft a recommended decision (grant / deny) with rationale citing the specific criterion.
checklist.done: a recommended grant/deny decision with a cited 164.526(a)(2) criterion is on the case.

checklist.step: Apply the restriction decision criteria (for RESTRICTION cases)
actions: Determine whether the request is a mandatory-grant case: disclosure to a health plan for payment/operations purposes, where the item/service was paid in full out-of-pocket, per 164.522(a)(1)(vi).
For non-mandatory requests, assess operational feasibility against treatment, payment and coverage obligations.
Draft a recommended decision (grant / deny / partial) with rationale.
Where granted, define the exact scope of the restriction (which data, which recipients, which purpose).
checklist.done: a recommended decision with defined restriction scope (if granted) is on the case.

checklist.step: Route the recommended decision to Privacy Counsel for review
actions: Review the Data Privacy Steward's rationale against the cited regulatory criterion.
For denials, confirm the denial letter draft states the basis, the member's right to submit a statement of disagreement, and the complaint process.
For restriction grants, confirm the scope is operationally enforceable (i.e., can actually be flagged in source systems).
Approve or send back for rework with specific required changes.
checklist.done: the decision and any denial letter carry Privacy Counsel's approval before communication to the member.

checklist.step: Communicate the decision to the member within the statutory window
actions: For amendments, send the grant confirmation or the approved denial letter within 60 days of the receipt date (or the extended date if an extension was issued).
For restrictions, send the grant or denial decision without undue delay, tracked against the internal 30-day SLA.
Use the member's confirmed accommodated communication channel per any active alternative-communication request.
Log the communication date and channel on the case.
checklist.done: the member has a logged decision communication inside the statutory window, on the accommodated channel.

checklist.step: Issue a compliant 30-day extension notice where the 60-day amendment clock cannot be met
actions: No later than day 60, determine whether the amendment decision genuinely cannot be completed on time.
Draft the extension notice in writing, stating the specific reason for delay and the new decision date (no more than 30 additional days).
Send the extension notice to the member before day 60 elapses.
Only one extension is permitted per request — log the extension use on the case to prevent a second.
checklist.done: any extended amendment case has a written, timely extension notice with a specific reason and new date, and only one extension used.

checklist.step: Amend the record and append it where the amendment is granted
actions: In the source system holding the designated record set, add the amendment as a linked appendage — never delete or alter the original entry.
Ensure the amendment identifies the changed information and the date of the amendment.
Confirm the record now displays both the original and the amendment to any future viewer.
Log the system, record identifier and amendment date on the case.
checklist.done: the amendment is appended to the record without deleting the original, and the case cites the system and record identifier.

checklist.step: Notify identified downstream recipients of a granted amendment
actions: Pull the accounting-of-disclosures log for the record to identify persons/entities who received the unamended PHI and who the member (or the plan) identifies as needing the correction.
Send each identified recipient the amendment notice within a reasonable time of the grant.
Log each notification's recipient, date and method on the case.
Where the member identifies additional recipients, add and notify them even after initial closure.
checklist.done: every identified downstream recipient has a logged, dated amendment notification.

checklist.step: Enforce a granted restriction in every relevant system
actions: Flag the restricted data element or disclosure type in the source system(s) per the defined restriction scope.
Confirm downstream extracts, reports and disclosure processes respect the flag (e.g., claims data feeds exclude the restricted item from the excluded recipient).
Test the flag with a sample disclosure scenario matching the restricted purpose.
Log the enforcement configuration and test result on the case.
checklist.done: the restriction flag is active in every relevant system and verified with a test scenario.

checklist.step: Log a statement of disagreement where the member submits one after a denial
actions: Accept and log any statement of disagreement the member submits after an amendment denial, without a length limit.
Attach the statement (or the plan's rebuttal, if any, per 164.526(d)) to the designated record set alongside the original request.
Confirm any future disclosure of the disputed information includes the statement of disagreement where the member requests it.
Log the attachment date on the case.
checklist.done: any submitted statement of disagreement is attached to the record and included in future disclosures on request.

checklist.step: Track the case against the SLA and escalate at the reminder thresholds
actions: Monitor the case queue's day-45/day-55 (amendment) and day-20 (restriction) reminder flags.
For any case approaching its deadline without a decision drafted, escalate to the Data Privacy Steward's manager.
Confirm the escalation results in a decision or an extension notice before the deadline.
Log the escalation and its resolution on the case.
checklist.done: every case approaching its deadline is escalated and resolved (decision or extension) before the deadline passes.

checklist.step: Close the case with full documentation
actions: Confirm the case carries the decision, Privacy Counsel approval, member communication date, and (for grants) the enforcement/notification evidence.
Set the case status to Closed with the final decision date.
Confirm no required field is blank before closing.
Notify the member's file/case record with the outcome summary.
checklist.done: the case is closed with all required documentation fields populated.

checklist.step: File the case evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the request, decision rationale, denial letter (if any), extension notice (if any) and notification confirmations into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year retention label from the case closure date.
Cross-reference the archive entry to the case number.
Confirm the archive is searchable by member identifier and case number.
checklist.done: the case evidence is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by member identifier and case number.

checklist.step: Report SLA performance to Privacy leadership monthly
actions: Summarize cases opened, closed, extended and any SLA breaches for the month.
Present the summary at the privacy governance meeting.
Identify any systemic cause of delay (e.g., a source system slow to enforce restriction flags) for corrective ownership.
File the summary alongside the month's evidence.
checklist.done: a monthly SLA performance summary is presented and filed.

testing.step: Build the population of amendment and restriction requests
actions: Extract every case tagged AMENDMENT or RESTRICTION with a receipt date inside the test period.
Reconcile the extract to the member correspondence log to confirm no request was received but never logged as a case.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the correspondence log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every case to a decision and communication date
actions: Match each case to its decision date and member communication date.
Confirm amendment decisions fall within 60 days (or 90 with a compliant extension) and restriction decisions within the internal SLA.
List unmatched or late rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a timely decision or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of denied requests and 100% of extended amendment requests.
Take a random sample of 20 granted requests, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers all denials and extensions.

testing.step: Re-perform the decision criterion on sampled cases
actions: Independently apply the 164.526(a)(2) or 164.522(a) criterion to each sampled case's facts without reading the original rationale first.
Compare to the recorded decision; any difference is an exception.
For denials, confirm the letter states the basis, statement-of-disagreement right and complaint process.
Note findings on the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent re-performance note and any difference is logged.

testing.step: Trace granted amendments to the appended record
actions: Open the source system record for each sampled granted amendment.
Confirm the amendment is appended (not substituted) and dated.
Confirm the original entry remains intact and visible.
Capture the system screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled granted amendment is confirmed appended without deletion of the original.

testing.step: Trace downstream amendment notifications
actions: For each sampled granted amendment, pull the accounting-of-disclosures log to identify prior recipients.
Confirm each identified recipient has a logged notification with date and method.
Flag any identified recipient with no notification as an exception.
Note findings on the workpaper.
testing.done: every identified downstream recipient for sampled amendments has a confirmed notification or a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify enforcement of granted restrictions
actions: For each sampled granted restriction, check the source system for an active restriction flag matching the defined scope.
Run or review a test disclosure scenario to confirm the restricted data was actually excluded.
Flag any restriction not technically enforced as an exception, escalated as a potential compliance breach.
Capture the system configuration into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled granted restriction is confirmed technically enforced, or flagged as a breach-level exception.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory deadline math for the sample
actions: Recompute days from receipt date to decision/communication date for each sampled case.
For extended amendment cases, confirm only one extension was used and the extension notice was sent before day 60.
Flag any case exceeding 60 (or 90 with a valid extension) days, or the internal restriction SLA, without escalation on file.
Log recomputation results on the workpaper.
testing.done: no sampled case exceeds its statutory or internal deadline without a logged, escalated exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a case per exception with the case number, member identifier (redacted in the workpaper) and the specific gap.
Assign a root cause (intake delay, wrong criterion applied, enforcement gap, missed notification) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; for any restriction found unenforced, treat as a reportable compliance breach requiring self-assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next month's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a case, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance SLA threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who worked no sampled case, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
